oa_vfyp9y.headline: A New Way to Pick the Best Model for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
oa_vfyp9y.hook: Researchers created a simple score that predicts how well any unsupervised domain‑adaptation model will perform on new target data, using only a few labeled source examples and a tiny unlabeled target sample. The score works by measuring how much the model’s predictions shift when that small target batch is added, letting it rank models almost as accurately as if full labels were available. This breakthrough could finally let engineers compare UDA methods fairly and pick the best one for real‑world tasks.
oa_vfyp9y.visual: a laptop screen showing a source‑domain photo of street cars labeled with bounding boxes on the left half and an unlabeled target‑domain night‑time street scene on the right half

oa_1bkhp34.headline: Takoma Park Runs First End‑to‑End Verifiable Election with Privacy
oa_1bkhp34.hook: In November 2009, Takoma Park, Maryland, let voters use Scantegrity II, a cryptographic voting system that lets anyone check that their vote was counted correctly while keeping the ballot secret. It was the first time a binding government election used an end‑to‑end verifiable method with ballot privacy, proving that strong security and voter anonymity can coexist in a real election. The successful run showed that advanced math can protect democracy without sacrificing trust.
oa_1bkhp34.visual: a close‑up of a voter’s hand marking a Scantegrity II ballot with a special invisible ink pen

oa_apr07p.headline: Real-Time Feeder Monitoring Transforms Smart Grid Reliability
oa_apr07p.hook: Researchers reviewed the latest systems that continuously monitor electricity feeders using sensors, communication networks, and data analytics to detect problems in real time. This shift from occasional manual checks to live monitoring can cut power losses and help prevent blackouts. The review shows how combining fast local processing, smart algorithms, and strong communication makes the grid smarter and more reliable.
oa_apr07p.visual: a sleek sensor device clamped onto a high-voltage power line with data streaming to a control room screen

oa_apr07v.headline: ESP32-Powered Voice Control System Brings Smart Home Automation
oa_apr07v.hook: Researchers built a low‑cost smart‑home controller using an ESP32 microchip that listens to voice commands and talks to the cloud. The system lets users turn lights, fans, or appliances on and off just by speaking, without needing expensive proprietary hubs. In tests, it responded quickly and reliably, showing how accessible voice‑controlled automation can be for everyday homes.
oa_apr07v.visual: a hand issuing a voice command to a compact ESP32 board connected to a smart light bulb

oa_1mfwk7n.headline: Agentic AI Survey Introduces Dual-Paradigm Framework
oa_1mfwk7n.hook: Researchers looked at the booming area of agentic AI and noticed that people often confuse today’s learning‑based systems with older rule‑based programs, which muddies the conversation. They created a straightforward two‑part framework that splits agents into those that learn from data and those that follow explicit rules, giving a common language to compare approaches. This clearer view helps engineers and decision‑makers see where the technology is headed and how to build smarter, more reliable autonomous systems.
oa_1mfwk7n.visual: a delivery drone hovering over a bustling city street

oa_vpm4p6.headline: Evaluating LSB Steganography Across Image Formats for Data Hiding
oa_vpm4p6.hook: Researchers tested how well the simplest pixel‑tweaking method hides data in PNG, JPEG, and BMP files, measuring how much information can be stored before the image looks noticeably altered. They found that lossless formats like PNG keep the secret intact with minimal distortion, while JPEG’s compression quickly erases the hidden bits.
oa_vpm4p6.visual: a side‑by‑side comparison of a PNG, JPEG, and BMP image each with a hidden text overlay visible as slight color shifts

oa_gppjrc.headline: SOAR Telescope Reveals Thousands of Close Binary Star Measurements
oa_gppjrc.hook: Using speckle interferometry on the 4.1‑meter SOAR telescope, astronomers measured the positions and brightness differences of over 5,300 star pairs, some as close as a tiny fraction of an arcsecond. These observations sharpen our view of nearby binary systems, helping refine stellar masses and evolution models. The dataset includes hundreds of previously unpublished measurements from before 2024.
oa_gppjrc.visual: the SOAR telescope’s open dome under a Milky Way‑filled sky

oa_1yy1l7j.headline: AI Kernel Keeps Observation, Assumptions, and Revision Paths Separate
oa_1yy1l7j.hook: Researchers built a new AI component called the World Model Kernel that forces the system to spell out what it saw, what it assumed, any leftover uncertainties, and how it might change its mind before giving an answer. By keeping these steps visible, the AI can explain its reasoning instead of hiding them behind a single guess. This could make AI safer and easier to trust in critical tasks.
oa_1yy1l7j.visual: a robotic hand holding a clear glass sphere filled with floating sticky notes labeled 'Observed', 'Assumed', and 'Revised'

oa_lxaqk0.headline: Survey Maps Security, Privacy, and Standards for the Coming 6G Era
oa_lxaqk0.hook: Researchers reviewed dozens of upcoming 6G proposals to see how they plan to protect data as billions of devices, edge servers, and AI algorithms join the network. They found that while new encryption and AI‑driven threat detection are promising, many privacy safeguards and global standards are still missing. The survey highlights where the field is heading and what gaps need to be filled before 6G rolls out.
oa_lxaqk0.visual: a futuristic cityscape with interconnected drones, smart sensors, and glowing data streams linking to a central 6G tower

oa_1td7chm.headline: Electronic Palm Achieves Crosstalk‑Free Pressure And Temperature Sensing
oa_1td7chm.hook: Researchers built a biomimetic electronic palm that splits sensing tasks among specialized units, eliminating interference between pressure and temperature readings. This design lets the hand detect both stimuli with high precision across large arrays, paving the way for more realistic touch in robots. The result is a sensor skin that could let machines feel objects as delicately as a human hand.
oa_1td7chm.visual: a silicone electronic palm pressing gently on a ripe strawberry

oa_1mfwmmt.headline: Survey Covers Knowledge and Dataset Distillation for LLMs
oa_1mfwmmt.hook: Researchers surveyed recent work on compressing huge language models using knowledge distillation—teaching smaller models from big ones—and dataset distillation—creating tiny synthetic datasets that capture the essence of massive training data. These techniques can cut compute and storage needs dramatically, making powerful AI more accessible on everyday devices. The survey highlights remaining challenges like preserving reasoning abilities and scaling to trillion‑parameter models.
oa_1mfwmmt.visual: a smartphone screen showing a tiny AI model icon next to a massive data center silhouette

oa_gah38b.headline: How Edge and Cloud Team Up to Power Smarter Apps
oa_gah38b.hook: Researchers surveyed the latest ways edge devices and cloud servers share AI workloads to cut latency and save energy. They show how splitting tasks between nearby sensors and distant data centers lets smartphones run complex models without draining the battery. The result is a roadmap for faster, greener smart‑city and industrial applications.
oa_gah38b.visual: a smart factory floor with autonomous robots communicating with a distant data center via glowing fiber‑optic links

oa_1wxekog.headline: When Silence Speaks: A New Index Measures What Unsaid Words Might Mean
oa_1wxekog.hook: Researchers built a tiny score called the Disclosure Terrain Index that tells you when someone's silence can be taken as a weak hint that something is absent. The score looks at how costly or risky it would be for a person to speak up; if speaking up is cheap, silence means less, but if it's expensive, silence counts a bit more as evidence. This gives auditors, journalists, or even chatbots a quick way to judge whether to trust a lack of comment as a clue, turning a gut feeling into a simple number.
oa_1wxekog.visual: a lone figure hesitating before a microphone in a dimly lit room, with a faint speech bubble hovering empty

oa_197l5j.headline: Designing Low-Power Chips for Deep Learning
oa_197l5j.hook: Researchers explored ways to make deep neural network processors use less energy without sacrificing speed. By tweaking circuit design and data flow, they cut power draw significantly for common AI tasks. The result could help run sophisticated models on phones and edge devices.
oa_197l5j.visual: a close-up of a neuromorphic processor chip with visible gold interconnects

arxiv_1e8v0az.headline: Rethinking ISO 26262 Controllability for Self‑Driving Cars
arxiv_1e8v0az.hook: The classic ISO 26262 safety framework assumes a human driver can intervene when something goes wrong. For autonomous vehicles, that assumption falls apart, so researchers broke down the controllability factor into two new ideas: how well the system can transfer control and how predictable its actions are. This shift lets safety experts judge AVs more fairly and could shape future regulations.
arxiv_1e8v0az.visual: a self‑driving car stopping at a crosswalk as pedestrians cross a city street

oa_1ng2ctv.headline: Review Maps the Evolving Landscape of Zero Trust Architecture Research
oa_1ng2ctv.hook: Researchers combed through hundreds of papers to map how zero trust ideas have shifted from theory to practice. They found that while the concept promises stronger security, real-world deployment still struggles with complexity and integration. The review highlights where the field is heading and what questions remain unanswered.
oa_1ng2ctv.visual: a padlock overlaying a network diagram with interconnected nodes

arxiv_nytipv.headline: Even The Best Generative Models Hallucinate, Study Shows
arxiv_nytipv.hook: Researchers redefined hallucinations in AI as moments when a model's guess has no real‑world cause behind it. They showed that even the most accurate possible algorithms still make these baseless guesses, guaranteeing a minimum rate of hallucination for any data. The result means hallucinations are built‑in to learning, not just a flaw to be erased.
arxiv_nytipv.visual: a vintage telescope pointed at a night sky where a bright star is missing

arxiv_12yz2ct.headline: How Well Do Multimodal AI Models Know Their Own Limits?
arxiv_12yz2ct.hook: Researchers took several advanced models that can read both images and text and checked how well their confidence matches their actual performance on jobs like captioning pictures and answering visual questions. They discovered that many of these models tend to be overconfident, which could cause problems in critical areas like medical diagnosis or self‑driving cars.
arxiv_12yz2ct.visual: a self-driving car's dashboard display showing a pedestrian outline with a question mark overlay

arxiv_1yazkj2.headline: Gradient-Based Prompt Tuning Boosts Diffusion Model Image Quality
arxiv_1yazkj2.hook: Researchers turned prompt writing into a gradient‑driven search, nudging words until the diffusion model’s output matches the description more closely. This approach finds better prompts without exhaustive trial‑and‑error, giving users higher‑quality images that follow their intent.
arxiv_1yazkj2.visual: a sleek workstation with a holographic keyboard where typed words float upward and morph into a vivid landscape on a transparent screen

arxiv_xk890m.headline: Blockly2Hooks Enables Visual Smart Contracts On XRP Ledger
arxiv_xk890m.hook: Researchers built Blockly2Hooks, a tool that lets anyone create smart contracts for the XRP Ledger by snapping together Google Blockly blocks like a visual programming language. This lowers the barrier for everyday users to deploy contracts for payments, NFTs, or automated agreements without writing code. The result is a drag‑and‑drop way to bring blockchain functionality to anyone with a browser.
arxiv_xk890m.visual: a hand arranging colorful Blockly puzzle blocks on a laptop screen displaying the XRP Ledger logo

arxiv_13jqmwf.headline: A Simple Trick Lets AI Learn From Any Number of Data Types At Once
arxiv_13jqmwf.hook: Researchers built a lightweight method that can align representations from text, images, audio, sensor streams, and more without needing paired examples for every combination. By contrasting each modality against a shared reference, the approach scales to unlimited data types while staying simple enough to plug into existing models. The result is a single embedding space that lets robots, medical systems, or video apps understand and transfer knowledge across modalities they’ve never seen together before.
arxiv_13jqmwf.visual: a quadruped robot stepping over rubble while projecting holographic icons of a speech bubble, a musical note, and a video frame above its back

arxiv_15n7ox4.headline: Shared Control Tested for Critical Driving Maneuvers
arxiv_15n7ox4.hook: Researchers let drivers and automation share steering during emergency lane changes and hard braking, measuring how well the combined system avoids collisions. They found that when the car gently nudges the wheel while the driver stays alert, reaction times improve and crash risk drops. The result shows a practical way to make self‑driving aids feel safer without taking full control away from the person behind the wheel.
arxiv_15n7ox4.visual: a sedan's steering wheel moving slightly under automated assistance while the driver's hands hover nearby

arxiv_6tnq76.headline: A New Primal‑Dual Lens Clarifies How Transformers Build Attention
arxiv_6tnq76.hook: Researchers turned the design of transformer attention into a primal‑dual optimization problem, letting them derive attention formulas from first principles. This view reveals why certain attention patterns work well and offers a systematic way to invent new ones that could improve language and vision models. The approach bridges the gap between heuristic tricks and solid mathematical grounding, promising more reliable and interpretable AI systems.
arxiv_6tnq76.visual: a mathematician drawing dual geometric shapes on a chalkboard next to a glowing transformer network diagram

arxiv_fpi292.headline: Bayesian Trust Shields Multi‑Agent Tracking From Compromised Agents
arxiv_fpi292.hook: Researchers examined how teams of sensors share data to track moving targets, then designed a Bayesian approach that lets each sensor judge the trustworthiness of its peers. Even when some sensors are hijacked and send false information, the method can still correctly decide whether a target is present. This means critical intelligence networks can stay reliable despite adversaries trying to slip in compromised agents.
arxiv_fpi292.visual: a flock of drones flying over a battlefield with one drone glowing red to indicate a compromised agent

arxiv_1rf9q8e.headline: Scene-Driven Exploration Boosts Android GUI Model Coverage
arxiv_1rf9q8e.hook: Researchers created a method that guides automated testers to focus on what users actually see on screen, letting them click through many more app pages than before. This produces richer maps of how an app’s screens connect, revealing hidden navigation paths. The improved maps help developers catch bugs faster and designers understand complex flows.
arxiv_1rf9q8e.visual: a smartphone screen displaying a vibrant app interface with highlighted buttons and arrows tracing a user’s path through multiple screens

arxiv_1ujia7b.headline: Formal Tool Checks That Masked Crypto Code Behaves Like the Original
arxiv_1ujia7b.hook: Researchers built an automated checker that compares a masked version of a cryptographic routine with its plain version, proving they produce the same results despite the added noise. This matters because masking is supposed to stop hackers from reading power leaks, but only if the masked code still works correctly. The tool can catch subtle bugs that would otherwise slip through, giving developers confidence that their side‑channel defenses don’t break the algorithm.
arxiv_1ujia7b.visual: a split‑screen laptop display showing the original cryptographic algorithm on the left and its masked version on the right, with a checkmark highlighting equivalence

arxiv_1puy6bz.headline: Logic‑Boosted AI Models Learn To Ground Abstract Concepts In Vision
arxiv_1puy6bz.hook: Researchers taught large language models to write simple programs that tell vision systems how to spot abstract ideas like “justice” or “freedom” in pictures. By adding logical rules, the AI can reason about concepts that aren’t directly visible, opening the door to machines that understand meaning beyond pixels. This step could let future assistants interpret complex scenes the way humans do.
arxiv_1puy6bz.visual: a transparent tablet screen showing a flowchart linking the word 'justice' to images of courtroom scenes

arxiv_1nagers.headline: New Testing Method Finds Compiler Bugs in Relaxed Memory Models
arxiv_1nagers.hook: Researchers built a tool that runs the same multi-threaded program through a compiler and then checks whether the allowed outcomes under the hardware's relaxed memory model match those possible from the original source code. When a mismatch appears, it signals a compiler bug that could cause subtle race conditions only visible in concurrent executions. This approach catches bugs that traditional testing misses, helping make compilers safer for real-world parallel software.
arxiv_1nagers.visual: a dual-pane code view showing source and compiled code with diverging thread arrows

arxiv_16k44pz.headline: Implicit Redundancy Boosts Self-Healing in Cyber-Physical Systems
arxiv_16k44pz.hook: Researchers found that hidden backup pathways already present in the hardware of cyber‑physical systems let the machines automatically reroute tasks when parts fail or are hit by an attack. This built‑in redundancy keeps the system running without adding extra components or waiting for a human fix. The approach could make factories, power grids, and other critical infrastructure far more resilient to unexpected glitches.
arxiv_16k44pz.visual: a factory robotic arm smoothly moving around a damaged joint while continuing its assembly task

arxiv_1xq1hyg.headline: LLM Frameworks Streamline Power‑System Coding From Routine to Novel
arxiv_1xq1hyg.hook: Researchers created LLM‑driven tools that turn plain‑language requests into working power‑system code, handling everything from routine data‑processing scripts to novel control algorithms. By automating the coding step, these frameworks let engineers spend less time debugging syntax and more time designing cleaner, more reliable energy systems.
arxiv_1xq1hyg.visual: a laptop displaying colorful power‑system code next to a miniature model of a power grid

arxiv_1qqq5je.headline: How Drivers Follow Self‑Driving Cars vs Human‑Driven Ones in Lyft Data
arxiv_1qqq5je.hook: Researchers pulled thousands of real‑world driving moments from Lyft’s open self‑driving car data, comparing how people drive behind robotaxis versus ordinary cars. They discovered that drivers leave noticeably more space when trailing an autonomous vehicle, suggesting a built‑in wariness of the machines. This gap could smooth traffic or create bottlenecks as self‑driving cars become common.
arxiv_1qqq5je.visual: a sedan trailing a self‑driving Lyft car on a city street at dusk

arxiv_gpdtxl.headline: Most CHERI-Ported Memory Allocators Fall to Security Tests on Morello
arxiv_gpdtxl.hook: Researchers took several open-source memory allocators and ran them on Arm's Morello board, which uses CHERI hardware capabilities to protect memory. They then tried a set of new attacks designed to bypass those protections and found that every allocator except one leaked or corrupted data. The result shows that even with strong hardware safeguards, allocator design still matters for real-world security.
arxiv_gpdtxl.visual: a researcher's hand holding a small circuit board labeled Morello with glowing CHERI capability tags

arxiv_tn4xbj.headline: How Ready Are People for Fully Driverless Cars?
arxiv_tn4xbj.hook: Researchers surveyed thousands of drivers across several countries to gauge trust, safety concerns, and willingness to ride in fully autonomous vehicles. They found that while many appreciate the promise of fewer accidents, a significant share remains uneasy about giving up control. The results highlight a clear gap between technological readiness and public acceptance that could shape how self‑driving cars roll out.
arxiv_tn4xbj.visual: a self-driving car stopped at a crosswalk with pedestrians waiting

arxiv_cvnvux.headline: AR Boosts Control of Vibration Exciters for Structural Tests
arxiv_cvnvux.hook: Researchers used augmented reality overlays to let engineers see and adjust vibration exciter settings in real time, replacing manual dials. This approach makes structural dynamics tests faster and more precise, especially in hard-to-reach lab or field setups. The result is a more intuitive way to probe how buildings and bridges respond to shakes.
arxiv_cvnvux.visual: an engineer wearing AR glasses while pointing at a vibrating metal plate on a test rig

arxiv_1tngp28.headline: Secure Key Exchange Protects Remote-Controlled Robots from Cyber Attacks
arxiv_1tngp28.hook: Researchers designed a protocol that lets a remote controller and a mobile robot agree on a secret encryption key while anyone listening can only see useless data. This keeps the robot’s commands safe from hackers who might try to seize control in factories, hospitals, or disaster zones. The scheme works even if the attacker can observe the whole exchange, making the robot resilient to sophisticated cyber‑attacks.
arxiv_1tngp28.visual: a wheeled robot navigating a warehouse aisle while a bright encrypted signal pulses from a remote controller in the operator's hand

arxiv_1mrj63p.headline: SysML Extension Enables Early Testing of Cyber‑Physical Systems
arxiv_1mrj63p.hook: Researchers built a modeling language based on SysML that lets engineers check both simulated and real‑world versions of cyber‑physical parts before building them. It helps spot design flaws early, saving time and money by showing whether a component can be reused across different systems. The result is a clearer path from concept to prototype, turning vague ideas into testable plans.
arxiv_1mrj63p.visual: a split‑screen showing a virtual drone model on one side and its real‑world counterpart flying side by side

arxiv_1afte1a.headline: Can Java Taint-Analysis Tools Find Bugs in Kotlin Code?
arxiv_1afte1a.hook: The researchers ran several Java-based taint analyzers on a suite of real-world Kotlin Android apps to see how many security flaws they could spot. They found that the tools catch most classic Java-style vulnerabilities, but miss issues that rely on Kotlin-specific features like null-safe calls, extension functions, and coroutines. This shows that reusing Java analysis works surprisingly well, yet Android developers still need Kotlin-aware extensions for full coverage.
arxiv_1afte1a.visual: a laptop screen showing Kotlin code with red arrows highlighting data flow from user input to a sink

oa_195jat.headline: Transit-Radial-Velocity Method Tracks Close-In Small Planet Evolution
oa_195jat.hook: Researchers built a model that uses both transit dips and stellar wobbles to study how small planets near their stars change over time. By combining these two measurements, they can infer the planets' makeup and how much atmosphere they lose without relying on guesses from a single technique. The approach gives a clearer picture of which close-in worlds might retain conditions suitable for life.
oa_195jat.visual: a small rocky planet transiting its host star while a spectrometer measures the star's wobble

oa_1yv8s0t.headline: How Machine Learning and IoT Are Transforming Crop Farming Monitoring
oa_1yv8s0t.hook: They gathered research showing how field sensors send data to smart programs that can warn farmers about dry spots or disease before it spreads. By turning those alerts into simple actions—like adjusting irrigation or applying fertilizer only where needed—growers can save water, cut costs and harvest more.
oa_1yv8s0t.visual: a farmer checking a tablet that shows a color-coded map of a wheat field while a small drone with attached sensors flies overhead

oa_bxkqto.headline: Prompt Injection Attacks on AI Systems: Risks and New Defenses
oa_bxkqto.hook: Researchers surveyed dozens of studies to map out how attackers can trick language models with malicious prompts, turning harmless chatbots into tools for data theft or harmful actions. They found that even simple text tweaks can bypass safeguards, exposing a hidden weakness in AI that powers everything from customer service bots to coding assistants. Understanding these tricks is the first step toward building AI that can resist being fooled.
oa_bxkqto.visual: a laptop screen showing a chat window with a highlighted malicious prompt overriding the AI's response

oa_1cg6bv4.headline: Genetic Overlap Reveals Shared Roots Across 14 Psychiatric Disorders
oa_1cg6bv4.hook: Researchers examined DNA from thousands of people diagnosed with fourteen different psychiatric conditions, searching for genetic variants that appear more often than chance. They discovered that most of the genetic risk is shared, especially between disorders like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, pointing to common biological pathways. This finding could change how we think about diagnosing and treating mental illness.
oa_1cg6bv4.visual: a human brain silhouette composed of fourteen interlocking colored puzzle pieces

oa_1lbgzg0.headline: Immune and Metabolic Signals Trigger Mitochondria-Driven Membrane Burst
oa_1lbgzg0.hook: Researchers found that when the body’s immune system and metabolism send certain signals, mitochondria can punch holes in a cell’s outer membrane, causing it to burst. They named this process mitoxyperiosis. Learning how it works could help explain tissue damage in infections and inflammation and suggest new treatment angles.
oa_1lbgzg0.visual: a mitochondrion releasing reactive molecules that puncture a cell membrane

oa_1tghvmj.headline: Plant Bioactives: From Extraction to Immunity and Health Benefits
oa_1tghvmj.hook: Researchers gathered hundreds of studies on plant-based compounds — from how they’re pulled out of leaves and fruits to what they do in our bodies. They show these molecules can strengthen immunity, improve nutrition, and even be used to make healthier foods. The takeaway? Everyday plants might hold powerful tools for fighting disease and boosting well‑being.
oa_1tghvmj.visual: a mortar and pestle grinding fresh green leaves, releasing a bright green liquid into a glass beaker

oa_lvja8a.headline: How Macrophage Switching Shapes Disease and Therapy
oa_lvja8a.hook: Macrophages are immune cells that can change their behavior to either heal tissue or drive inflammation, depending on signals they receive. Researchers reviewed how these switches work at the molecular level and how they contribute to diseases like cancer, arthritis, and Alzheimer’s. Understanding these mechanisms opens the door to drugs that can reprogram macrophages for therapeutic benefit.
oa_lvja8a.visual: a macrophage cell splitting into two distinct shapes, one spiky and one rounded, against a tissue background

oa_16uvo67.headline: Why a Fixed Human Lifespan Might Threaten Civilization's Future
oa_16uvo67.hook: The paper argues that knowing we will probably die before 120 pushes societies to favor short‑term rewards over long‑term investments. This mindset weakens institutions that need decades to pay off, such as climate mitigation or AI safety research. Over generations, the resulting decay could become a bigger existential threat than any sudden catastrophe.
oa_16uvo67.visual: an hourglass half‑filled with sand, its lower bulb spilling over a miniature cityscape

oa_1w7sm0o.headline: AI Combines Genomics, Proteomics, and Imaging to Guide Cancer Treatment
oa_1w7sm0o.hook: Researchers used artificial intelligence to pull together data from genes, proteins, metabolites and medical scans from thousands of cancer patients. By finding patterns across these layers, the AI predicts which therapies will work best for each individual. This could turn a mountain of confusing lab results into clear, actionable treatment plans.
oa_1w7sm0o.visual: a doctor holding a tablet that shows a vibrant, layered map of genes, proteins, and tumor images intertwining

oa_qgust4.headline: Mitophagy Protects Cells by Removing Damaged Mitochondria in Disease
oa_qgust4.hook: Researchers reviewed how cells use mitophagy to toss out busted mitochondria, keeping the power plants healthy. When this cleanup falters, it can fuel neurodegenerative disorders, heart disease, and even cancer. Understanding these mechanisms points to new ways to boost cellular health and treat illness.
oa_qgust4.visual: a damaged mitochondrion being engulfed by a green autophagosome inside a cell

oa_4uz67v.headline: How mTOR Controls Cell Growth And Why It Matters For Treating Disease
oa_4uz67v.hook: Researchers mapped how the mTOR pathway senses nutrients and stress to switch cell growth on and off, revealing new details about its wiring. Understanding these switches helps explain why mTOR drugs are being tested for cancer, diabetes, and even aging, opening doors to more precise treatments.
oa_4uz67v.visual: a close-up of a fluorescently labeled mTOR protein complex inside a living cell

oa_1had1bc.headline: New Safety Guidelines for Low‑Intensity Brain Stimulation from ESBS
oa_1had1bc.hook: Experts have refreshed the safety and ethical rules for using weak electric currents on the scalp to tweak brain activity. The updated guide helps anyone using these devices stay safe while exploring possible boosts to mood, focus, and recovery.
oa_1had1bc.visual: a close‑up of a flexible electrode pad gently pressed against a person's forehead

oa_1opdfeh.headline: Fasting Improves Mitochondrial and Endothelial Health in Aging Vessels
oa_1opdfeh.hook: Researchers put older mice on intermittent fasting regimens and measured how well their brain‑feeding blood vessels worked. They found that fasting restored mitochondrial energy production and tightened the lining of those vessels, improving blood flow and barrier integrity. The results suggest a simple dietary tweak could help protect cognition as we age.
oa_1opdfeh.visual: a cross‑section of a mouse cerebral artery showing bright mitochondria pulsing inside endothelial cells

oa_6yzapf.headline: Childhood Emotional Abuse Tied to Suicidal Thoughts in College
oa_6yzapf.hook: Researchers surveyed college students about childhood emotional abuse, their difficulty identifying feelings, and suicidal thoughts, while also measuring exercise habits. They found that trouble processing emotions partly explains why abuse leads to suicidal ideas, but regular physical activity weakens both the direct link and this emotional pathway. This suggests that staying active could help break a dangerous chain from early trauma to self‑harm.
oa_6yzapf.visual: a college student running on a campus track at sunrise, headphones on, with a folded journal tucked under arm

oa_m2go4.headline: When AI Helps Us Cope: Offloading Thoughts or Overloading Minds?
oa_m2go4.hook: Researchers surveyed how people use AI assistants, predictive alerts, and therapy chatbots to manage daily stress, finding that these tools can both lighten mental load and create new dependencies. The results show that while AI can offload routine thinking, it may also flood users with constant notifications and expectations, reshaping how we cope with challenges.
oa_m2go4.visual: a young adult holding a smartphone displaying a chatbot interface, with thought bubbles of to-do lists and stress icons

oa_56z0wl.headline: How Eating Less Triggers Longevity Genes Across Yeast, Worms, and Mice
oa_56z0wl.hook: Researchers looked at organisms ranging from yeast to mice that were fed fewer calories and found they all activated a similar set of genes linked to slower aging and better health. This shared response shows that the benefits of eating less are built into our biology across evolution, not just a quirk of one species. Understanding these common pathways could point to ways to help people stay healthier longer without extreme dieting.
oa_56z0wl.visual: a split‑image showing a yeast colony, a tiny nematode worm, and a mouse each next to a reduced‑portion food dish

oa_1xtvrqg.headline: Designing Digital Media For Kids Boosts Learning And Well‑Being
oa_1xtvrqg.hook: Researchers looked at how television, apps, video games and voice assistants influence kids' development, finding that when these tools match children's cognitive and emotional stages they can boost learning and mental health. But when the same platforms are built to maximize clicks and ad revenue, they often hurt attention, sleep and self‑esteem. The message is clear: thoughtful design, not just more screen time, decides whether digital media helps or harms the next generation.
oa_1xtvrqg.visual: a child sitting on a rug surrounded by floating icons of a TV, tablet, game controller and smartphone, each emitting a soft glow

oa_1ve4hha.headline: Microplastics Lurking in Your Lipstick: What It Means for Your Skin
oa_1ve4hha.hook: Researchers scanned dozens of everyday cosmetics — from foundations to mascaras — and found tiny plastic particles hiding in the formulas. These microplastics can slip through the skin's outer layer, raising questions about what they might do once inside. Understanding this hidden exposure could change how we think about the safety of our beauty routines.
oa_1ve4hha.visual: a close-up of a lipstick bullet speckled with tiny glitter-like plastic fragments

oa_mokk9x.headline: How Resistance Training Prescription Shapes Muscle Growth and Strength
oa_mokk9x.hook: Researchers combined findings from many review articles to see how different resistance‑training routines influence muscle size and strength in healthy adults. They concluded that programs using challenging weights performed regularly lead to clear gains in both muscle growth and functional ability. The result is a practical, evidence‑backed guide that anyone can use to build effective workouts.
oa_mokk9x.visual: a close‑up of hands gripping a barbell during a deadlift

oa_cjrhbn.headline: Weight Self‑Stigma Fuels Appearance Anxiety in Female College Students
oa_cjrhbn.hook: Researchers surveyed hundreds of female undergraduates to see how feeling ashamed about their weight relates to worries about looks. They found that weight self‑stigma not only directly raises appearance anxiety but also shapes distinct groups of students who experience it differently. Understanding these patterns could help campuses design better mental‑health support.
oa_cjrhbn.visual: a female college student looking at her reflection in a dormitory mirror while holding a notebook

oa_papjv5.headline: How AI Is Reshaping the Future of Drug Discovery and Molecular Design
oa_papjv5.hook: Researchers surveyed how machine‑learning models are now predicting promising drug candidates, designing new molecules, and prioritizing targets faster than traditional methods. By integrating AI with massive biological data, the approach can significantly shorten early‑stage discovery and open doors to treatments for diseases that have lacked effective therapies. The review highlights both breakthrough successes and the remaining hurdles before AI‑designed medicines reach patients.
oa_papjv5.visual: a robotic arm holding a glowing molecule model over a digital network of interconnected nodes

oa_pgnvmq.headline: How Bioactive Compounds Shape the Skin Microbiome and Fight Disease
oa_pgnvmq.hook: Researchers looked at how natural and synthetic bioactive compounds can change the bacteria living on our skin. Shifting this microbial balance can calm inflammation, worsen it, or even affect how quickly skin ages. The findings suggest that what we apply topically could be a powerful tool for treating acne, eczema, and other skin conditions.
oa_pgnvmq.visual: a close-up of human skin dotted with glowing bacterial colonies and a droplet of plant extract

oa_a4j3je.headline: Linking Obesity Solutions to Climate Action
oa_a4j3je.hook: Researchers reviewed the latest science showing that tackling obesity and climate change can use overlapping strategies, such as shifting diets toward plant‑based foods and redesigning cities for active travel. These approaches cut greenhouse‑gas emissions while also lowering rates of weight‑related disease. The review highlights why policies that address both crises together could be more effective than tackling them separately.
oa_a4j3je.visual: a bustling urban street filled with cyclists and pedestrians alongside a farmer’s market stall displaying fresh vegetables

oa_19tn00g.headline: How Gilgamesh Turns Heroic Strength on Its Head
oa_19tn00g.hook: The study re‑reads the Epic of Gilgamesh, showing that the king’s supposed strength is actually undermined while the wild companion Enkidu embodies true resilience. By flipping the usual hero‑sidekick dynamic, the text asks what it really means to be strong in a world of gods and mortals. This fresh angle reveals how ancient literature wrestles with power, vulnerability, and the limits of divinity.
oa_19tn00g.visual: a stone tablet showing Gilgamesh kneeling while Enkidu stands defiantly beside a lion

oa_xijreo.headline: How Liver X Receptors Influence Aging and Age‑Related Diseases
oa_xijreo.hook: Researchers reviewed how Liver X receptors, which sense cholesterol‑related molecules, connect to the biological processes that drive aging. By linking LXR activity to hallmarks like inflammation, metabolic decline, and cellular stress, the review highlights a potential lever for slowing age‑related disease. Targeting these receptors could open new routes to extend healthy lifespan.
oa_xijreo.visual: a liver cell nucleus highlighted with bright spots showing Liver X receptor activation

oa_u9tfn8.headline: NR and Berberine: Boosting Mitochondria to Fight Aging
oa_u9tfn8.hook: Researchers looked at how nicotinamide riboside, a form of vitamin B3, and berberine, a plant compound, each help cells recharge their energy factories. Both compounds raise NAD+ levels and activate a key energy sensor, which can improve mitochondrial function and reduce wear and tear linked to aging and disease. The findings suggest that combining them might offer a simple way to support cellular health as we get older.
oa_u9tfn8.visual: a mitochondrion inside a cell glowing like a tiny power plant

oa_rro4b9.headline: Tech, Renewables, and Policies Driving G‑7 Sustainability
oa_rro4b9.hook: Researchers examined G‑7 countries to see whether investing in new technology, expanding renewable energy, and enforcing strict environmental rules actually improves sustainability. They found that stronger policies and more renewable energy use are linked to better environmental outcomes, while the impact of tech innovation is less certain. This helps policymakers know which actions are most effective for meeting climate goals.
oa_rro4b9.visual: a wind farm on a coastal hill overlooking a city skyline

oa_fwfe8x.headline: What Makes a Post‑Growth Model Work? Key Elements Revealed
oa_fwfe8x.hook: Researchers looked at many sustainability ideas to figure out what a real post‑growth plan must include — clear goals, ways to measure progress, and steps that separate quality of life from endless economic growth. They found that missing any of these pieces makes the plan slip back into old growth‑first thinking. The outcome is a simple checklist that leaders can use to check whether a scenario truly puts people and the planet ahead of profit.
oa_fwfe8x.visual: a group of people planting trees in a reclaimed urban lot

oa_1auc2uf.headline: How Public Participation Shapes Urban Green Infrastructure Success
oa_1auc2uf.hook: Researchers reviewed dozens of studies on city green projects to see how involving residents changes outcomes. They found that when people help decide where and how parks, rain gardens, or green roofs are built, those projects work better and last longer. The study shows that listening to community values and giving them real influence can turn good ideas into lasting urban improvements.
oa_1auc2uf.visual: a diverse group of neighbors planting trees in a city sidewalk rain garden

oa_wjdcvv.headline: Endurance and Resistance Training Reshapes Muscle Gene Activity
oa_wjdcvv.hook: Young adults followed a combined running and weight‑lifting program for several weeks. Researchers then sampled tiny pieces of their thigh muscles to see which genes switched on or off in each cell type. The training rewired the pattern of gene activity, boosting signals for energy and repair while damping inflammation, showing how mixing cardio and strength fine‑tunes muscle at a molecular level.
oa_wjdcvv.visual: a person jogging on a treadmill while holding dumbbells

oa_qv09if.headline: How AI And Smart Grids Could Revolutionize City‑Wide Heating Networks
oa_qv09if.hook: Researchers surveyed dozens of studies to see how smart sensors, AI, and new business models could turn old‑fashioned city heating networks into flexible, low‑carbon services. This matters because most urban heating still relies on centralized fossil fuel plants and lacks the data sharing needed to respond to demand or renewable supply. The review shows that combining digital tools with updated policies could let neighborhoods buy heat like electricity, cutting emissions and giving residents more control.
oa_qv09if.visual: a municipal heating plant with solar panels on its roof and a digital dashboard displaying real-time temperature flows

oa_l3ezbx.headline: How Short Bursts vs Steady Exercise Affect Brain Energy in Aging Rats
oa_l3ezbx.hook: Researchers placed older rats on either a sprint‑style workout or a steady jog for several weeks, then measured how their brain cells used fuel. The interval training boosted key energy markers more than the continuous routine, suggesting short, intense bouts could help keep aging brains sharper.
oa_l3ezbx.visual: an older rat sprinting on a treadmill while a timer flashes

oa_1i6svtd.headline: Cosmetic Dermatology’s Emerging Role in Extending Healthspan
oa_1i6svtd.hook: The paper points out that living longer doesn't automatically mean living healthier, distinguishing total lifespan from the years we stay free of serious illness. It then argues that cosmetic dermatology—think lasers, fillers, and skin‑care routines—could help preserve skin health and, by extension, overall vitality as we age. By linking what we do for our skin to broader aging processes, the authors suggest that aesthetic treatments might contribute to extending our healthspan.
oa_1i6svtd.visual: a dermatologist performing a laser skin resurfacing procedure on a patient's face while a chart showing lifespan versus healthspan hangs on the clinic wall

oa_giuimy.headline: How Friendly Bacteria in Creams Could Transform Your Skin Health
oa_giuimy.hook: Researchers reviewed how adding prebiotics, probiotics, and postbiotics to creams influences the skin's microbial community and barrier function. They found that these ingredients can help good microbes thrive while calming inflammation and strengthening the skin’s defenses. The takeaway? Your daily moisturizer might soon double as a microbiome‑boosting treatment.
oa_giuimy.visual: a hand applying a white moisturizer to forearm, with tiny glowing bacteria visible on the skin

oa_1uq7r3r.headline: Adapting to Water Scarcity for Sustainable Farming in Sub‑Saharan Africa
oa_1uq7r3r.hook: Researchers surveyed farms across Sub‑Saharan Africa to see how growers are responding to worsening water shortages. They found that simple tactics—like capturing rainwater, using low‑flow drip lines, and planting drought‑resistant varieties—can raise crop output while cutting water use. The results show which mixes of these tools work best in dry versus semi‑dry zones, giving governments and NGOs a clear guide to boost food security and inch toward the Zero Hunger goal.
oa_1uq7r3r.visual: a farmer adjusting a drip‑irrigation line in a millet field under a bright sky

oa_vl7rv5.headline: Community Pharmacists' Knowledge Gaps in Treating Chronic Skin
oa_vl7rv5.hook: Researchers surveyed community pharmacists to see how well they understand and advise on topical treatments for long‑term skin problems like eczema and psoriasis. They found many pharmacists feel unsure about dosing and side‑effects, highlighting a need for more targeted training. Improving this knowledge could help patients get safer, more effective care at the pharmacy counter.
oa_vl7rv5.visual: a pharmacist holding a tube of topical cream while talking to a patient with visible rash on their arm

oa_1vesfdr.headline: Engineering Your Skin's Microbiome for Custom Skincare
oa_1vesfdr.hook: Researchers are tweaking the microbes that live on our skin to create lotions that match each person’s unique bacterial makeup. By bioengineering friendly bacteria, they aim to boost skin health, reduce irritation, and cut down on waste from one‑size‑fits‑all products. The result could be skincare that feels like it was made just for you, because it literally is.
oa_1vesfdr.visual: a petri dish displaying a pattern of multicolored bacterial colonies forming a smiley face

oa_apc8fh.headline: How Mechanical Tension Fuels Muscle Growth and Busts Common Myths
oa_apc8fh.hook: The paper reviews how lifting weights creates tension in muscle fibers, which triggers the biological signals that make muscles grow bigger and stronger. It then unpacks popular beliefs—like the need for extreme soreness or specific rep ranges—showing which are backed by evidence and which are just myths that can waste effort.
oa_apc8fh.visual: a close-up of a human bicep muscle bulging under a weighted barbell

oa_18os4jg.headline: Weight Load Doesn't Predict Muscle Growth in Arms vs Legs
oa_18os4jg.hook: Researchers had 20 healthy young men lift weights three times a week for several weeks, measuring muscle size in their arms and legs. They found that how heavy the weights were didn't explain why some people's muscles grew more than others, suggesting individual biology plays a bigger role. This shifts focus from just lifting heavier to understanding personal factors that drive gains.
oa_18os4jg.visual: a split-screen image showing a muscular arm and a muscular leg side by side

oa_1j19olz.headline: Melatonin’s Hidden Power: From Sleep Aid to Skin Healer
oa_1j19olz.hook: Researchers reviewed how melatonin, best known for regulating sleep, also acts as a powerful antioxidant and immune modulator in the skin. They found that applying melatonin topically can help reduce inflammation, protect against UV damage, and improve conditions like eczema and psoriasis. These insights open the door to new melatonin‑based creams and gels for everyday skin care.
oa_1j19olz.visual: a hand applying a melatonin‑infused cream to a patch of skin

oa_1nx0epr.headline: Lipid Nanoparticles Boost Skin Healing For Aging And Disease
oa_1nx0epr.hook: Researchers made tiny fat‑based particles that can carry soothing and moisturizing ingredients deeper into the skin. These particles stay on the surface and help repair the skin’s natural barrier in problems like psoriasis, eczema and dry, aging skin. Lab tests showed they reduced redness and boosted moisture better than standard creams.
oa_1nx0epr.visual: a droplet of lipid nanoparticle merging with cracked, dry skin

oa_yk9fwo.headline: High-Intensity Interval Training Boosts Heart Fitness and Enlarges the
oa_yk9fwo.hook: Researchers swapped athletes’ usual endurance routines for short, all‑out bursts during the off‑season. After weeks of this training, participants’ VO₂ max increased and their heart’s left ventricle showed measurable thickening, indicating stronger pumping power. The results reveal that even brief, intense sessions can reshape the heart for better performance when regular training pauses.
oa_yk9fwo.visual: a sprinter exploding from starting blocks while a heart‑rate monitor spikes

oa_136zm99.headline: Short Bursts, Different Rest: How HIIT Tweaks Boost Taekwondo Fitness
oa_136zm99.hook: Researchers had teen taekwondo champions perform high‑intensity intervals with either short or long recovery breaks while keeping the total workout time identical. After several weeks, the group with the shorter rests showed greater gains in kicking speed and leg power than the longer‑rest group, revealing that the way effort is sliced can matter as much as the effort itself. This suggests coaches can sharpen athletes’ explosiveness without adding extra practice time.
oa_136zm99.visual: a teenage taekwondo athlete executing a high kick, sweat droplets flying, with a visible timer showing work and rest intervals

oa_1trttlq.headline: High-Intensity Interval Training Boosts Strength and Mobility in Seniors
oa_1trttlq.hook: Researchers asked a group of adults over 65 to perform short, intense bursts of exercise on a stationary bike, followed by brief recovery periods, three times a week for two months. By the end of the study, participants could walk faster, stand up from a chair more easily, and reported feeling stronger during everyday activities like carrying groceries or climbing stairs.
oa_1trttlq.visual: an older adult sprinting on a treadmill while a trainer watches

oa_wqbrrb.headline: How Alternating Heavy And Light Wushu Training Boosts Anaerobic Power
oa_wqbrrb.hook: Researchers had participants switch between intense bursts of Wushu moves and lighter technique drills to see how it affects short‑burst power. The goal was to find out if this mix‑and‑match approach can improve the kind of explosive fitness needed for quick strikes and fast footwork. If it works, martial artists could get a simple way to boost their sprint‑like power without extra equipment.
oa_wqbrrb.visual: a Wushu practitioner delivering a powerful jumping kick in a training hall

oa_tlwvip.headline: Why Skin Loses Its Shield As We Age
oa_tlwvip.hook: Researchers looked at many studies to see how aging skin slowly loses its power to protect, heal, and stay moist. They found that our genes and the natural wear‑and‑tear of cells, together with sun and pollution, make the skin thinner and less able to block irritants. Knowing this helps scientists create better creams and treatments for older skin.
oa_tlwvip.visual: a close‑up of an elderly person's hand with deep wrinkles resting on a soft towel

oa_qlps6i.headline: Niacinamide May Reduce Wrinkles and Boost Skin Barrier
oa_qlps6i.hook: Researchers looked at dozens of studies on niacinamide and found it helps the skin retain moisture, smooth out fine lines, and fade dark spots. Because it’s cheap, well‑tolerated, and works on several aging signs at once, the vitamin B3 derivative could be a simple addition to everyday skincare routines.
oa_qlps6i.visual: a close-up of healthy facial skin with a subtle glow and visible pores

oa_1jcvddn.headline: Aerobic Warm-Up Fails to Boost Muscle Growth in Older Adults
oa_1jcvddn.hook: Researchers tested whether a short bout of aerobic exercise before weight lifting helps older adults gain more muscle. They found that the cardio warm-up made no extra difference in muscle size after weeks of training.
oa_1jcvddn.visual: an older man performing a bicep curl with dumbbells in a gym

arxiv_olyyrq.headline: How Impact IRR Applies Portfolio Theory To Measure Social Returns
arxiv_olyyrq.hook: Researchers took Modern Portfolio Theory, the classic tool for balancing risk and reward in stocks, and adapted it to measure the social and environmental payoff of impact investments. By defining an impact internal rate of return, they give investors a single number that blends financial gain with measurable good. This could help the $1.6 trillion impact market compare funds as easily as comparing mutual funds.
arxiv_olyyrq.visual: a scale balancing a gold coin on one side and a sprouting seedling on the other

arxiv_1nfmyst.headline: Monte Carlo Study Shows How Copper Powders Affect Ion Sputtering Yields
arxiv_1nfmyst.hook: Researchers built a detailed computer simulation that tracks how individual copper grains in a powder respond when hit by krypton ions. They found that the rough, loose structure of the powder changes the amount of material knocked away compared to a flat copper surface. This insight helps explain sputtering on planetary surfaces and improves control of thin‑film coating processes.
arxiv_1nfmyst.visual: a close-up of copper powder granules illuminated by a focused beam of krypton ions

arxiv_14bw6g9.headline: How Brain‑Sensing Tech Could Boost Focus and Treat Disease
arxiv_14bw6g9.hook: Researchers surveyed the latest advances in devices that read brain signals, process them in real time, and deliver tiny electrical pulses to influence neural activity. They show how closing the loop between sensing and stimulation can restore movement after injury, sharpen attention in healthy users, and open new ways to treat psychiatric conditions. The roadmap highlights challenges in safety, ethics, and making the tech wearable for everyday life.
arxiv_14bw6g9.visual: a user wearing a flexible brain‑sensor headset reaching for a coffee cup

arxiv_vbnamk.headline: How Peer Pressure Shapes Stock Prices on Financial Networks
arxiv_vbnamk.hook: Researchers simulated traders who care about how their returns stack up against their peers, placing them on a branching network that mimics a family tree of connections. They found that this simple social pressure can cause prices to swing dramatically, creating boom‑and‑bust cycles even when no new news arrives. The result shows that peer influence alone can move markets.
arxiv_vbnamk.visual: a network of interconnected nodes shaped like a tree, with tiny trader figures at each node watching a fluctuating stock chart

arxiv_mrk277.headline: Observing Market Trades Can Skew Portfolio Risk Estimates, Study Shows
arxiv_mrk277.hook: Researchers examined how an investor who never buys or sells can still estimate his portfolio’s risk by watching the trades of others in the market. They found that using only those observed trades can make the classic Markowitz variance either far too low or far too high, which can lead to serious misjudgments about safety.
arxiv_mrk277.visual: a trader's hand hovering over a stock ticker displaying rapid trade numbers while a laminated portfolio sheet lies unchanged beside a coffee mug

arxiv_187gpgr.headline: HardTaint Lowers DTA Overhead With Selective Hardware Tracing
arxiv_187gpgr.hook: Researchers created HardTaint, a system that uses built‑in CPU tracing to watch only the most critical data flows in a running program. By limiting hardware monitoring to those flows, HardTaint avoids the massive slowdown that usually makes dynamic taint analysis impractical for production use. In tests, it caught real security bugs while adding only a tiny fraction of the overhead of traditional taint checkers.
arxiv_187gpgr.visual: a silicon CPU die illuminated with bright tracer lines tracing specific data paths

arxiv_1chmgv5.headline: Femtomolar NT-proBNP Detection in Saliva Using Graphene-Based Aptasensor
arxiv_1chmgv5.hook: Researchers created a tiny sensor that can spot the heart‑failure marker NT‑proBNP in saliva at concentrations a thousand times lower than in blood. By dipping a graphene‑coated probe into artificial saliva, they achieved femtomolar‑level sensitivity, opening the door to quick, non‑invasive heart checks at home or clinics.
arxiv_1chmgv5.visual: a graphene-coated sensor tip dipped into a droplet of artificial saliva

arxiv_1o5ye6j.headline: How Past Market Trades Shape Investors' Real Returns
arxiv_1o5ye6j.hook: Researchers traced how the average size and swing of investors' real returns depend on the patterns of today's trades and the history of past trades. They built three layers of approximation to link those market movements to what people actually pocket when they sell. The result shows that yesterday's market noise can quietly shape today's profit or loss.
arxiv_1o5ye6j.visual: a trader's hand gripping a glowing ticker tape that winds into a fading line chart of past market prices

oa_184shlb.headline: JWST's JADES Survey Maps Early Galaxies Across Two Deep Fields
oa_184shlb.hook: Using about 770 hours of JWST time, researchers imaged and took spectra of the GOODS-S and GOODS-N regions to capture the faintest galaxies ever seen. This lets astronomers trace how galaxies grew from the early universe to the peak of star‑forming activity known as cosmic noon. The survey reveals thousands of distant galaxies, some shining just a few hundred million years after the Big Bang.
oa_184shlb.visual: a deep-field infrared image packed with countless faint galaxies
